meta.title: Well-known variants
meta.status: Draft selection, for a biology teacher to review.
meta.coordinates: Positions count letters from the start of the chromosome, as in gene-regions.json. startBp is inclusive and starts at 0; endBp is exclusive. Letters are on the forward strand.
notes: A variant is a place where people's DNA differs. referenceLetters are the letters in the reference genome from startBp to endBp, and match gene-regions.json. variantLetters replace them in the variant version; an empty string means the letters are missing.
The reference genome is one example of human DNA, not the normal or most common one. For some variants here the variant letters are the more common version.
For a gene on the "-" strand the change reads as the complementary letter in the gene's own direction: a forward-strand T to A is an A to T in the gene.

effect was worked out from the letters and coding parts in gene-regions.json. position counts amino acids from the first one, methionine, as 1. Older textbooks often count from the amino acid after it, so their numbers can be one lower.
frequency counts gene copies among the people in gnomAD: copiesWithVariant out of copiesCounted, and share is one divided by the other. Each person has two copies of most genes.
gnomAD is not a balanced sample of the world's people. A variant can be much more or much less common in a particular place or family than the share here.
How common a variant is says nothing about any one person. Summaries describe well-established science in plain words and are not medical advice.

variants.title: The sickle cell change
variants.summary: One letter differs, and one amino acid of beta-globin changes with it. People with two copies of this version have sickle cell disease. People with one copy are usually well and are partly protected against malaria.

variants.title: Haemoglobin C
variants.summary: This change is in the letter next to the sickle cell change and alters the same amino acid in a different way. The result is a version of haemoglobin called haemoglobin C.

variants.title: A switch for lactase
variants.summary: This letter lies inside the MCM6 gene and changes no protein. It sits in a switch that controls the neighbouring gene, LCT. People with this version usually keep making lactase as adults. Other changes close by have the same effect in other parts of the world.

variants.title: An early stop in ACTN3
variants.summary: One letter differs and turns the code for an amino acid into a stop signal, so the protein is cut short. People with two copies of this version make none of this muscle protein and are healthy.

variants.title: Bitter taste receptor: first change
variants.summary: One of three common changes in the bitter taste receptor. Together they make the two common versions of the gene, which affect whether a person can taste the bitter chemical PTC.

variants.summary: One of three common changes in the bitter taste receptor. Together they make the two common versions of the gene, which affect whether a person can taste the bitter chemical PTC.

variants.title: MC1R: a red hair change
variants.summary: One of the changes in MC1R most often linked to red hair. People who carry two such changes, the same or different, usually have red hair.

variants.summary: One of the changes in MC1R most often linked to red hair. People who carry two such changes, the same or different, usually have red hair.

variants.title: The most common cystic fibrosis change
variants.summary: Three letters are missing, so one amino acid is left out of the CFTR protein. People with two copies of this version have cystic fibrosis. People with one copy are carriers and are well.
